The <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>heroic being dedicated to awakening</gloss> <term>Mahasattva</term> <gloss>great being</gloss> also brings the six <term>paramitas</term> <gloss>perfections</gloss> to complete fulfillment. Such a being also draws near to <term>sarvakara-jnata</term> <gloss>all-encompassing knowledge or omniscience</gloss>.

Furthermore, Subhuti, when a Bodhisattva Mahasattva practices the six perfections, if they see sentient beings born in the four ways—born from an egg, born from a womb, born from heat and moisture, or born miraculously—they should reflect in this way: 

In whatever way I manifest complete and perfect awakening in the unexcelled state of a Buddha, in that Buddha-field, the three modes of birth—from an egg, from a womb, and from heat and moisture—shall not occur and shall not exist. Instead, all sentient beings shall be born miraculously. In that manner, I shall practice the six perfections. I shall completely purify the Buddha-field. I shall bring sentient beings to full maturity. 

Subhuti, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva who practices in this way also brings the six perfections to complete fulfillment. They also draw near to all-encompassing knowledge.

<summary>This page describes the Bodhisattva's vow to eliminate inferior modes of birth in their future Buddha-field, ensuring all beings are born miraculously. It emphasizes that such compassionate aspirations lead the practitioner toward complete omniscience.</summary>
